title: What Is To Be Done?
author: V.I. Lenin
shortDescription: Lenin's seminal work on political organization, arguing that working-class political consciousness requires systematic theoretical education rather than pure trade unionism.
subject: Party Organization
context: Published in early 1902 while Lenin was in exile, What Is To Be Done? responded to sharp debates within Russian Marxism. Lenin argued against 'Economism' (the idea that workers should focus only on economic wage demands) and advocated for a centralized, disciplined organization of professional revolutionaries capable of operating under secret police repression.
relatesToToday: Explains why modern social movements, spontaneous protests, and hashtag activism often fade away without lasting change unless backed by organized, disciplined campaign structures, clear political strategy, and dedicated full-time organizers.
keyTakeaways: Trade-union consciousness is not enough: Spontaneous worker struggles naturally focus on immediate economic gains (wages and working conditions), but political socialist consciousness must be developed through education and theory.
Without revolutionary theory, there can be no revolutionary movement: Sound theoretical understanding is essential to prevent movements from being co-opted by reformist compromises.
Need for professional organization: Operating against powerful state and corporate forces requires dedicated, disciplined organizers rather than loose, amateur circles.
The press as a collective organizer: An independent political publication serves as a scaffold that unifies local struggles into a coordinated national movement.
